title: MatterGen: Property-Guided Generative Diffusion for Inorganic Crystals
whyItMatters: Shifts inorganic materials discovery from brute-force screening to inverse generative design—steering crystal structures directly toward target mechanical, magnetic, or electronic properties.
summary: Published in Nature (Vol. 639) with open-source weights and code, Microsoft Research's MatterGen is a joint diffusion model over atomic species, coordinates, and unit-cell lattices across the periodic table. Fine-tuned adapter modules steer crystal generation toward specified band gaps, magnetic densities, or bulk moduli, doubling the rate of stable, unique, novel candidates compared to prior generative models.
technicalHighlights: Jointly diffuses discrete atom types, fractional coordinates, and continuous lattice geometry.
Supports multi-property conditioning (e.g., high magnetic density + low supply-chain-risk elements).
Open-source release (MIT) catalyzed a wave of inverse-design crystal diffusion models.
caveats: An April 2026 Materials Horizons audit challenged the novelty of the flagship experimentally synthesized example (TaCr₂O₆, reported in 1972 literature and training sets), underscoring the gap between benchmark generation and genuinely unprecedented industrial materials.

scoreRationale.foundational: Established conditional crystal-diffusion as a clean paradigm for inverse inorganic materials design.
scoreRationale.ripple: Widely adopted as an open baseline across battery electrolytes, magnets, photovoltaics, and catalysis research.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature with open checkpoints, tempered by 2026 independent scrutiny over experimental novelty claims.
scoreRationale.velocity: Replaced million-structure DFT screening funnels with direct property-conditioned generation.
